top_story.headline: Former Rep. Eric Massa's committee says it is holding cash for legal fees over alleged forged House pay records and theft
top_story.dek: Filed Friday, October 2, in response to a September 2 Federal Election Commission letter about the committee's leftover funds.
paragraphs: Massa for Congress told the Federal Election Commission it has kept its cash on hand because of "pending legal matters that require a contingency fund for legal fees," and that it has done nothing else since ceasing operations. It says it will dispose of the excess funds and terminate once those matters are resolved. The filing doesn't say how much cash is involved. Form 99 submission.

The letter says the committee has informed the Justice Department, the House employment counsel's office and the House Ethics Committee of legal issues that may require representation before those bodies. It describes "documented proof of forgery of House pay records that resulted in the theft of tens of thousands of dollars by a former employee," which it says was uncovered during a multi-year investigation of what it calls "debunked allegations" against Eric Massa. It says the documents have been presented to those agencies and the matter remains unresolved. The letter names no employee and gives no dollar figure, and the claims are the committee's own.

sections.headline: Three House incumbents file Form 99 letters, two about refunding general-election money
paragraphs: All three letters were filed Friday, October 2. Two members say they are refunding contributions for a general election in which they are not on the ballot, and one answers a request about excessive contributions and foreign addresses.

items: Rep. David Scott (D-GA-13), committee David Scott for Congress, responding to review of the July Quarterly Report (April 1 to June 30): the committee acknowledges receiving contributions for a general election in which it is not participating and is issuing refunds, which will appear in its fourth-quarter report. Filing.

Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA-17), committee Ro for Congress Inc, responding to an August 30 Request for Additional Information about the July Quarterly Report: says all excessive contributions have been refunded, redesignated or reattributed with notices to contributors, and that for two donors with foreign addresses the committee obtained current passport copies and confirmed US citizenship. Filing.

Rep. Frederica S. Wilson (D-FL-24), committee Frederica S. Wilson for Congress: says general-election contributions were refunded in full on September 30, 2026, and will show on the October filing. Filing.

sections.headline: Five other Form 99 letters, one of them the Massa for Congress filing above
paragraphs: No new Requests for Additional Information (FRQ filings) surfaced in this window beyond those already reported in earlier editions. The new Form 99 letters from non-incumbent filers are below.

items: Massa for Congress (House candidate committee, former member): explains why it still holds cash; see the Top Story. Filing.

Fight On PAC (Iowa PAC), treasurer Cabell Hobbs: answers an October 1 Request for Additional Information on its August Monthly Report, saying it will file an amended Statement of Organization naming Team Hinson as a joint fundraising representative. Filing.
Steven Fuller for Congress (Colorado challenger, 5th District): a one-sentence note saying it has not raised or spent $5,000 and is covering its filing requirements. Filing.
Alaine Elizabeth Giuliani (presidential candidate committee, New York): "No monies to report for October Quarterly." Filed October 1. Filing.

Deliver Energize Succeed PAC: a paper Notification of Multicandidate Status, mostly illegible in the scan; the FEC's receipt page shows it was shipped overnight September 25 and received October 1. The FEC's index lists it as a Form 99 filed October 1. Filing.
